title: The Missed Trade
hook: Missing it isn’t a reason to rewrite it.

launchpad.outcome: Separate a pass from a miss, and find what actually failed without rewriting the entry model.

slides.headline: You came back at 10:04. It’s gone.
slides.line: Your plan: long on the retest of the PIL. The retest came while your phone was on silent in the other room.
chips: Alert set at the PIL retest
slides.q: Price is far above your planned entry. Now what?

options.label: Chase it now
options.sub: Get in before it runs more
options.say: That isn’t your setup any more. Your stop and target were built for the retest.

options.label: Find any reason to get in
options.say: That’s inventing an entry because you missed one.

options.label: Let it go
options.say: Yes. A missed trade costs nothing. A chase can.

slides.headline: “Next time I’ll enter earlier.” What actually failed?

options.label: The strategy
options.say: It produced exactly the trade it was supposed to.

options.label: The analysis
options.say: The read was right. Price reached the target.

options.label: The entry model
options.sub: I should enter before the retest
options.say: The retest came, exactly as planned. You weren’t there for it.

options.label: Access and attention
options.say: Yes. The method worked. The miss was access and attention.

slides.headline: A pass and a miss are different things.

cards.title: A pass is a decision
cards.text: You chose not to participate, for a reason.

cards.title: A miss is an execution gap
cards.text: A valid, planned trade that didn’t get placed.

cards.title: Fix the gap, not the method
cards.text: An alert you can hear. Being at the screen in your window.

slides.dayli: Don’t change the method just because hindsight gave you perfect vision.

takeaways: A pass is a decision. A miss is an execution gap.
If a valid setup was simply missed, don’t rewrite the entry model.
remember: Don’t change the method just because hindsight gave you perfect vision.
